newsitem.title: CHINA: China to let HK handle some diplomatic issues.
newsitem.headline: China to let HK handle some diplomatic issues.

text.p: China's envoy in Hong Kong said on Wednesday Beijing will allow the former British colony to handle a number of its own diplomatic issues.

Ma Yuzhen, the Hong Kong Commissioner of China's Foreign Ministry, said in his first interview with local media that the territory's constitution, the Basic Law, grants the local government powers to handle certain diplomatic issues.

"I can't interfere with those diplomatic affairs that the central government has already authorised the Special Administrative Region (SAR) government to deal with under the Basic Law," he told Hong Kong television.
China resumed sovereignty over Hong Kong on July 1, when the former British colony became a Special Administrative Region of China.
Hong Kong runs all its own domestic affairs but foreign affairs and defence are strictly in Beijing's hands.
But Ma was quoted by local television as saying Beijing would authorise the local administration to handle more diplomatic affairs.
For example, Beijing has already authorised Hong Kong to hold talks with other countries on visa-free access arrangements, he said.
But issues such as the establishment of other countries' diplomatic missions in Hong Kong or visits by foreign warships to the territory fell under his charge, he said.
Ma, a former Chinese ambassador in Britain, said Sino-British relations had improved recently.
"The Chinese government does not only protect British investment in Hong Kong, through our policy and the Basic Law, but we also welcome more British investment in China," he said.

But Ma said China regretted that Britain, which made the territory a port of first asylum for Vietnamese boat people, did not solve the problem of Vietnamese migrants in Hong Kong before the empire retreated.
"The British government declared Hong Kong as the port of first asylum. This was what the British government imposed on Hong Kong," he said.
"As long as this problem has not been solved, the Chinese government thinks that all relevant parties should continue to have the responsibility to resolve this completely," he said.
He said the post-colonial government could deport illegal Vietnamese immigrants according to its law.
More than 3,000 Vietnamese are still in the territory's detention camps. China had demanded all camps should be emptied by the handover.
